cells.tense: You are close to people and still your own person inside it.
cells.ask: Say one true thing to someone you've been protecting from it, and let it land without softening it after.
cells.core:
You can feel what someone else feels and stay yourself while you do it. That is the shape of connection when it is working here — you are not managing them and you are not merging. You notice what is going on with them, and you also know where you end.

The care that produced this did not drain you. You stayed in contact while you carried the weight, and both things held at once. The cost is that people start handing you what they cannot carry themselves, and you are good at holding it. Keeping the exchange mutual — sometimes receiving out loud — is what keeps it alive. The closeness stays a two-way street instead of a job you are quietly doing alone.
cells.sheetLine: You stay close and stay whole.
cells.verb: tending what is alive until it can stand without you
cells.place: beside someone, close enough to feel what they feel and stay separate

cells.tense: You are bracing for the connection to fade and working hard to hold it.
cells.ask: Pick one person you are quietly managing and ask them what they want from you, then let the answer stand.
cells.core:
Where this looks right is simple: you feel what someone feels, you stay separate, and you let the two of you meet where you actually are. That is connection doing its work — different people, real contact, nobody absorbed.

Right now you are pitching forward into it. You feel what they might need before they have said it, you are already shaping yourself around a version of the relationship that has not happened, and the effort goes into that version instead of the one in front of you. The care itself is sound. The timing is what has slipped — your weight is somewhere ahead of where the two of you actually stand.
cells.sheetLine: You are steering a connection that hasn't happened yet.

cells.tense: You stopped offering yourself to people in a way that lands.
cells.ask: Pick one person and tell them something you want for yourself, not what you're doing for them.
cells.core:
You know how this feels when it is going well: people can feel you in the room. You know what matters to you, you say things plainly, and the connection is one you inhabit rather than watch from outside it.

What is happening now is quieter. You are present, but not reachable — private, practical, saying the safe half of things. The feeling did not leave; the form it used to take went missing. Underneath is care with no outlet, and trying harder at closeness will not reach it. Direction does: knowing again what you are moving toward, so people have something of yours to meet. When the light you follow is real, contact stops being effort and starts being ordinary.
cells.sheetLine: The warmth is still there. It's just not going out.

cells.tense: You are already growing something in common with people, without noticing you are doing it.
cells.ask: Name one shared thing you have been calling ordinary and say out loud that you built it.
cells.core:
This is how it runs: a group is warmer with each other, people keep showing up, conversations leave something behind that was not there before. Connection that produces things. And you are one of the people making it — not standing outside it, not just benefiting from what others arranged.

Yet you describe it as if it happened by itself. The care you put in does not announce itself, so it rarely gets counted. That is the release here: seeing what you made and saying so once, out loud. It is not pride. It just lets you keep at it without quietly carrying the whole thing alone.
cells.sheetLine: You built the thing you're calling ordinary.
